# Intake Brief: Static docs site for local browsing (VitePress)

**Priority: Low** | **Type: Chore** | **Assignee: Map**

> Discovered from MS-0MUNB54KU005084C as the deferred option (B). Producer
> answers 2026-10-17: still wanted (Q1=A); **navigation-first** use case
> (Q2=A); **local dev tool only**, no CI publishing (Q3=B).

## Headline

Add a VitePress static docs site over the existing `docs/game/` and
`docs/dev/` trees so developers and content authors can browse the docs with
sidebar navigation and rendered Mermaid locally (`npm run docs`); no CI
publishing is required.

## Problem statement

The repo ships docs as a flat, two-tree Markdown forest (`docs/game/`,
`docs/dev/`). Without a site, readers must navigate raw files and there is no
sidebar nav, no search, and no unified landing page. Mermaid fences in docs
(`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `the-build-gdd.md`) render only with a
Mermaid-aware viewer. A static docs site fixes browsing and renders Mermaid at
build time.

## Users

- **Developers** — need to browse game + dev docs with nav/search while
  working on the codebase.
  - *"As a developer, I want a docs site with sidebar navigation, so I can
    find the right doc faster without guessing file paths."*
- **Game designers / content authors** — need the gameplay reference plus the
  storyline graphs readable in place.
  - *"As a content designer, I want Mermaid diagrams rendered in the docs
    page, so the storyline shape is visible without a Mermaid tool."*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Docs site generator** — `vitepress` (MIT) is added as a devDependency
   and a `npm run docs` script serves the docs site locally
   (`vitepress dev docs`); the site root is `docs/` and covers both the
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/` trees with sidebar navigation. The
   `docs/.vitepress/` build output is git-ignored and the toolchain stays a
   devDependency only (it never enters the game bundle).
   *Metric: `npm run docs` starts a local server; `npm run docs:build`
   (`vitepress build docs`) exits 0 and emits a static site; `git status`
   stays clean after a build.*
2. **Navigation** — a sidebar (`.vitepress/config.ts`) lists the `docs/game/`
   and `docs/dev/` documents with clear audiences; every top-level `.md` in
   both trees is reachable from the nav (no orphaned docs).
   *Metric: a test asserts every `.md` under `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/` is
   covered by the sidebar config.*
3. **Mermaid rendering** — mermaid code fences in docs render to visible
   diagrams in the built site; the existing committed storyline SVGs
   (`docs/game/assets/storyline-graph-*.svg`) remain usable and are linked or
   embedded as today.
   *Metric: `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and `the-build-gdd.md`
   render with visible diagrams in the built site.*
4. **No link breakage / no migration** — existing files stay in place under
   `docs/game/` and `docs/dev/`; existing relative links between docs keep
   working; the `docs-path-drift` guard test stays green (no
   `docs/main-street/` or `example-games/main-street/` strings in the new
   VitePress config).
   *Metric: full suite passes including `docs-path-drift.test.ts`.*
5. **Testing/validation** — a pure config-scan unit test validates the docs
   build config (nav coverage + no forbidden paths) with no
   Playwright/browser requirement, and the full project test suite passes
   with the new changes.
   *Metric: the nav-coverage test runs in the `unit` project and asserts every
   top-level `.md` under both trees is listed in the sidebar; `npm test` exits
   0.*
6. **All related documentation is updated** — `docs/README.md` (and/or a new
   `docs/index.md`) documents the docs site plus the `npm run docs` /
   `npm run docs:build` commands, and the README reflects the new scripts.
   *Metric: `docs/README.md` or `docs/index.md` mentions `npm run docs`, and
   the project README documents the docs scripts.*
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.
8. **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages or docs CI workflow/job is added;
   the `docs` scripts are for local use and the existing game Pages deploy
   workflow is unchanged.
   *Metric: no new or modified workflow file references the docs build; the
   existing deploy workflow is untouched.*
9. **Permissive licence** — `vitepress` and every new plugin/dependency are
   permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0).
   *Metric: each new dependency's licence is checked and recorded in the
   implementation notes.*
10. **Remote-browser access is documented (WSL caveat)** — the docs pages
   state that `npm run docs` binds to `localhost` only, so a browser running
   outside the dev-server network namespace (the WSL case: server in WSL,
   browser on Windows) cannot load `http://localhost:<port>/`, and give the
   workaround: start the server with `npm run docs -- --host` and open the
   network IP address it prints. Documentation only — no behaviour change is
   required (producer audit rejection, 2026-10-23: "no need to fix this, just
   document it").
   *Metric: `docs/README.md` and `docs/index.md` both name the
   `npm run docs -- --host` invocation and the printed network-IP URL.*

## Constraints

- **Local-only, no CI** — no GitHub Pages workflow, no docs CI job
   (Q3=B). `docs` scripts are for local use; the existing game Pages deploy
   workflow is untouched.
- **Permissive licence** — `vitepress` (MIT) and any new plugin must be
   permissively licensed (MIT/Apache-2.0/CC0).
- **devDependency only** — the docs toolchain must not enter the game bundle.
- **No reorganisation** — files stay under `docs/game/` / `docs/dev/`; the
   two-tree structure and `docs/README.md` index remain.
- **Drift guard** — new VitePress files under `docs/` must not contain
   `example-games/main-street/` or `docs/main-street/` (scanned by
   `docs-path-drift.test.ts`).
- **Determinism/coverage** — the nav-coverage test must be stable and fast
   (no Playwright/browser requirement for the unit suite).

## Existing state (repo research)

- No docs-site generator present: devDeps include `vite`, `vitest`,
   `playwright`, `mermaid`, `sharp`, `tsx`, `vite-node`, but **no
   `vitepress`/`docusaurus`/`mkdocs`** anywhere in the repo or `core/`.
- `docs/` is plain Markdown: `docs/README.md` index, `docs/game/` (11 files +
   `storylines/` (5) + `assets/` with 5 storyline SVGs), `docs/dev/` (21 files +
   `assets/` (9) + `analysis/`).
- Mermaid fences exist in `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (:162),
   `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (:207, :617); the storyline graph
   ships as committed SVGs under `docs/game/assets/`.
- `docs-path-drift.test.ts` scans every text file under `docs/` for
   forbidden legacy paths; a `.vitepress/config.ts` (or `.mjs`) is a `.ts`
   text file and will be scanned — it must avoid those strings.
- Node v22.22.1 (VitePress requires Node ≥18 — satisfied).
- `.gitignore` has `dist/` and `dist-electron/`; VitePress build output
   (`docs/.vitepress/dist`) must be ignored (add `.vitepress` or
   `docs/.vitepress/dist`).

## Desired change

1. Add `vitepress` (devDependency) and a `docs` npm script.
2. Add `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` with sidebar nav for both trees
   (or `.mjs` if TS config is awkward with the repo's toolchain — prefer
   `.ts` since Vite toolchain is already TS).
3. Theme/plugin for Mermaid rendering (e.g. via the `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`
   or a mermaid pre-render step) so mermaid code fences become visible
   diagrams in the built site.
4. Add a nav-coverage test (`tests/main-street/`) asserting every top-level
   `.md` in both trees appears in the sidebar config, plus the drift-guard
   string check on the new config files.
5. Update `docs/README.md` (or add `docs/index.md`) to note the docs site and
   the `npm run docs` command.
6. Document the remote-browser caveat (WSL): `npm run docs` binds to
   `localhost`, which a Windows-hosted browser cannot reach from a WSL dev
   server; document `npm run docs -- --host` plus the printed network IP as
   the workaround (documentation only, no behaviour change — AC10).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**

- `./package.json` — **edit** `vitepress` and `vitepress-plugin-mermaid`
  devDependencies plus the `docs` / `docs:build` / `docs:preview` scripts.
- `docs/.vitepress/config.ts` — **new** VitePress config (title, sidebar,
  Mermaid plugin, `markdown.html: false`, dead-link allowances).
- `docs/.vitepress/sidebar.ts` — **new** sidebar generated from the Markdown
  tree on disk, so no document can be orphaned.
- `tests/main-street/docs-site-nav.test.ts` — **new** nav-coverage + drift-
  string test (runs in the `unit` project, no browser).
- `tests/main-street/docs-path-drift.test.ts` — **edit** existing drift guard;
  it now prunes the git-ignored `.vitepress/dist` + `.vitepress/cache` build
  output from its scan.
- `./.gitignore` — **edit** ignore the VitePress `dist/` and `cache/` output.
- `docs/README.md` — **edit** "Browsing these docs as a site" section (also
  the home for the AC10 remote-browser note).
- `docs/index.md` — **new** docs-site landing page (also carries the AC10
  remote-browser note).
- `./README.md` — **edit** document the `docs*` npm scripts and the docs tree.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUNB54KU005084C** — Render the storyline graph (Mermaid→SVG) — completed (v0.1.19); this item is its deferred option (B).
- **MS-0MUYLLYX80090370** — Link & document the rendered storyline graph — completed; embedded the SVG in the canonical doc and documented regeneration.
- **MS-0MUZK0OWJ000PQ2D** — Restructure documentation (two-tree split) — established `docs/game/` + `docs/dev/`.
- **MS-0MUNC8AOL0092BE5** — Fix stale `example-games/main-street` paths — owner of the `docs-path-drift` guard.
- **MS-0MUSY1M1F003IS47** — Editor host & read-only graph viewer (blocked) — may eventually consume the docs-rendered graphs.

## Assumptions

- The docs site is **local-only** (Q3=B): no CI build or Pages publishing is
  added; if publishing is wanted later it is a follow-up item.
- Navigation is the primary need (Q2=A); Mermaid fences are rendered in the
  built site (client-side rendering acceptable — see risk) and do not replace
  the committed `.mmd`/SVG pipeline.
- `nodemon`/live-reload behaviour from VitePress dev server is fine; no
  custom theme is needed beyond Mermaid support.

## Risks

- **Toolchain adoption (LOW–MED).** VitePress is Vite-native (repo already
  uses Vite), but its config adds a new docs toolchain. *Mitigation:*
  devDependency only; config kept small; no bundler changes.
- **Mermaid rendering approach (MED).** `vitepress-plugin-mermaid` renders
  client-side in the browser by default, not at build time; the item title
  says "at build time". *Mitigation:* either pre-render server-side (run the
  existing `mermaid` + Playwright render step during `docs:build`) or accept
  client-side rendering for the local dev use case (Q3=B); record the choice
  in the item at implementation.
- **Drift-guard interference (LOW).** New `.vitepress` files are scanned by
  `docs-path-drift.test.ts`. *Mitigation:* keep the forbidden strings out of
  new config; nav test covers coverage.
- **Scope creep risk.** Full-text search, versioning/multi-version docs,
  CI publishing, i18n, custom theming → out of scope; record as separate
  work items if requested.
- **Test determinism (LOW).** Nav test must not require a browser; keep it a
  pure config-scan unit test.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Still wanted?** Now that the minimal render step is shipped, is the
  larger static docs site still desired?
  - Options: (A) Still want it; (B) No longer needed.
  - **Recommended: (B).** Original problem solved by MS-0MUNB54KU005084C.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (A)** — still build the static docs
    site. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 — Primary use case?**
  - Options: (A) Better navigation/structure; (B) Mermaid-at-render for all
    docs; (C) Both.
  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (A)** — navigation-first; Mermaid
    rendering at build time remains in the title/scope but is not the sole
    driver. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 — Target audience / delivery?**
  - Options: (A) Internal/CI only (Pages); (B) Local dev tool (`npm run
    docs`); (C) Both.
  - **Recommended: (A).**
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): (B)** — local dev tool only; **no CI
    publishing**. Source: interactive reply.

> All three answers recorded in comment MS-C0MVBVDIK0006YSM7.

- **Q4 — WSL / remote-browser access** (raised by the producer's audit
  rejection, 2026-10-23).
  - Observation: `npm run docs` serves at `http://localhost:5174/` but that URL
    refuses connections in the producer's WSL setup (browser on Windows);
    `npm run docs -- --host` starts the server, `localhost` still fails, but
    the printed network IP addresses work.
  - **Answer (producer, 2026-10-23): document it, do not fix it.** Recorded as
    AC10 with a documentation-only metric.
  - Evidence: audit rejection recorded on this item (status `Partial`,
    author `rgardler`).

## Resolved questions

- **Build-time vs client-side Mermaid rendering — RESOLVED at implementation
  (2026-10-23).** The concern: the title says "render Mermaid docs at build
  time" while the Risks section permits client-side rendering for the
  local-only use case (Q3=B). Implementation chose **client-side rendering**
  via `vitepress-plugin-mermaid` (the proposed default), verified headlessly in
  Chromium — `core-rules-and-mechanics.md` renders 2 diagrams (stateDiagram +
  flowchart), `the-build-gdd.md` renders 1, zero page errors — and recorded the
  choice in comment MS-C0MVKSK0DQ0074SOP. The producer's 2026-10-23 audit
  raised no objection to the approach, so the question is closed and AC3 as
  written ("visible diagrams in the built site") stands.
- **WSL / remote-browser access — RESOLVED by the producer (2026-10-23).**
  `npm run docs` prints `http://localhost:5174/`, which a browser on Windows
  cannot reach from the WSL dev server, even with `--host`; the printed network
  IP addresses work. Producer's instruction: "There is no need to fix this,
  just document it." Recorded as **AC10** (documentation only). Evidence: audit
  rejection on this item, 2026-10-23.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-19 — `/skill:plan` run: effort/risk pre-check returned **skip**
  (Extra Small, Low risk), so no decomposition was performed. Six-stage
  review applied conservatively: AC alignment (AC1 now covers the gitignore
  and devDependency-only constraints; AC8 added for local-only/no-CI; AC9 for
  permissive licence; AC5/AC6 tightened to measurable criteria), completeness
  (added the existing `docs-path-drift.test.ts` guard to Key Files),
  testability (nav test pinned to the `unit` project, no browser), polish
  (fixed the `vitepress build docs` typo). Open Question raised on build-time
  vs client-side Mermaid rendering.
- 2026-11-04 — `/skill/plan` run (herdr downtime dispatch, session
  herdr-1793817702-1886894-21404). Effort/risk pre-check again returned
  **skip** (Extra Small, Low risk), so no decomposition: the item remains a
  single slice with no children. Six-stage review applied to the existing
  content **after** the first implementation landed (commit `582ab9e5`,
  merged to `dev`): AC alignment — added **AC10** for the producer's
  2026-10-23 audit finding (remote-browser/WSL access must be documented, no
  fix required) and added desired-change item 6 for it; completeness — Key
  Files converted to the canonical validated `**Key Files:**` form
  (`validate_key_files_format()` clean) and updated to the files actually
  touched (`docs/.vitepress/sidebar.ts`, `docs/index.md`, the drift-guard
  edit); sequencing — no children, so no dependency edges (AC10 is the only
  outstanding slice); scope sizing — unchanged, single deliverable; acceptance
  & testability — AC10 pinned to a documentation-only grep metric in both
  `docs/README.md` and `docs/index.md`; polish — the previously open
  build-time-vs-client-side Mermaid question moved to **Resolved questions**
  (client-side chosen and verified at implementation), and the producer's WSL
  answer recorded as appendix Q4. No open questions remain blocking planning.

# Intake Brief — End of game stats (MS-0MVAMU6OM008GJPV)

## Problem statement

The Main Street **Game Over** overlay currently presents only a *static*
end-of-run snapshot (per-player rows, score breakdown, challenges). Players
cannot see **how their economy evolved turn by turn**, so they cannot tell what
worked and what did not, or learn from a failed run. This item adds per-turn
history tracking to the game state and a **third column of end-of-game
graphs** (profit per turn, cash, businesses, staff and reputation at end of
turn), with the **cash-at-end-of-turn** figure surfaced on the Summary column
and a link to the detailed stats.

## Users

- **Main Street player at game over** — wants a visual run recap instead of
  just a final number.
  - *As a player, I want to see my cash, reputation, businesses and staff
    change turn by turn, so I can understand what worked and improve my next
    run.*
- **Competitive player** — wants the same trajectory for their own seat, so a
  loss against AI can be diagnosed.
- **Balance team / designers** — benefit from a deterministic, serialisable
  per-turn series they can inspect (and reuse for analytics).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Per-turn history captured.** A new `turnStatsHistory` series records one
   snapshot per completed turn — `{ turn, coins, reputation, score, profit,
   businesses, staff }` — where `profit` is the turn's net coin delta
   (reusing the existing `weekStartCoins` snapshot). The snapshot is recorded
   on **both** the deferred (`deferResourceApplication`) and legacy end-of-turn
   paths, and is never recorded twice for the same turn.
2. **Persistence.** `turnStatsHistory` is serialised in
   `MainStreetSerializedState` and restored by `deserializeMainStreetState`;
   legacy saves without the field load with an empty history (no crash, no
   fabricated data).
3. **Graphs.** The Game Over overlay renders a **third column** containing
   composed graphs for: **profit per turn**, **cash at end of turn**,
   **businesses at end of turn**, **staff at end of turn**, and **reputation
   at end of turn**.
4. **Summary cash line + link.** The Summary column shows the final
   **Cash at end of turn** figure, and provides a link/affordance to the
   detailed stats column.
5. **Both modes and layout.** The overlay works in single-player and
   competitive mode and fits the 1280×720 viewport without text clipping or
   vertical overflow; the existing Game State and Summary content is retained.
6. **Overlay conventions.** The new UI honours the established conventions:
   Phaser-free pure model for series data, `hudContainer` parenting, depths
   199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (interactive), everything pushed into
   `overlayObjects`; the overlay reads committed state only (no mutation),
   adds no animation (reduced-motion safe) and returns early in
   `scene.replayMode`.
7. **Testing.** Unit tests cover per-turn capture (both paths, no
   double-record), serialise/deserialise round-trip and legacy fallback, and
   the pure series model; browser tests assert the third column and the cash
   line render in both modes.
8. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Producer decisions (see Appendix):**
  - Target project is **`tce-main-street`** (the item was mis-filed in the
    ContextHub worklog; relocated as this item).
  - **Per-turn history = Option A.** The save game does **not** hold a full
    per-turn history — only the current-turn `weekStartCoins/Rep/Score`
    snapshot — so a new per-turn series must be added, **reusing the existing
    snapshot mechanism/pattern** (persisted alongside the save, legacy
    fallback).
  - **Charting = external charting library** (producer Q3 = B; e.g. Chart.js),
    not hand-rolled Phaser Graphics (A) or SVG-as-texture (C).
  - **No additional stats** beyond the five listed (producer Q4 = "No").
  - **Layout = add a third column** to the Game Over overlay (producer Q5),
    rather than a separate full-page stats screen.
- Game engine is **Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`**; overlay rendering lives in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`.
- External chart library integration with the Phaser canvas must not regress
  headless/Monte-Carlo runs or replay mode (chart module is skipped there).
- CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** (managed by the ship pipeline); no CI/CD
  pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- **Game Over overlay:** `showGameOverOverlay()` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — two columns (**Game State** /
  **Summary**) with a top band (title + end-reason headline) and the
  Play Again / Menu controls anchored at the panel bottom (panel is 900 px
  wide, laid out by `panelW` / `colW` / `colGap`). The pure, Phaser-free
  content model is `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts`
  (`buildGameOverPlayerRows`, `buildGameOverChallengeSummary`,
  `formatEndReason`).
- **Current-turn snapshot:** `state.weekStartCoins` / `weekStartRep` /
  `weekStartScore` are set in `executeWeekStart`
  (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`) and serialised in
  `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`. The per-turn net row
  (`appendTurnNetRow`, `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) derives the
  turn's deltas from that snapshot and logs
  `Turn <n> net: <deltas> (score: <delta>)`.
- **Ledger history:** `EconomyLedger.getHistory()`
  (`core/src/rule-engine/EconomyLedger.ts`, imported as
  `@rule-engine/EconomyLedger`) records *every mutation*, is **not
  serialised**, and is **not per-turn** — unsuitable as-is for the graphs.
- **Counts available at turn end:** businesses = non-null entries in
  `state.streetGrid`; staff = `state.staffCards.length`; cash/reputation =
  `state.resourceBank`; score = `state.finalScore`.
- **Precedent:** the Monte Carlo harness already captures a per-turn series
  (`economyHistory: [{ turn, coins, reputation, score }]`) in
  `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` for balance analytics — a useful shape to
  mirror.
- **Save/load:** `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState`
  in `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, with legacy fallbacks for absent
  fields.

## Desired change

1. **State.** Add a `TurnStatSnapshot` interface (`turn`, `coins`,
   `reputation`, `score`, `profit`, `businesses`, `staff`) and
   `turnStatsHistory: TurnStatSnapshot[]` to `MainStreetState`; initialise it
   to `[]` in `setupMainStreetGame` / `createCompetitiveState`.
2. **Capture.** Record one snapshot at the end of each completed turn —
   covering the **deferred** path (`finishDeferredTurnClosing`, after deltas
   are applied) and the **legacy** path — so the turn's net profit is computed
   against `weekStartCoins` exactly like `appendTurnNetRow`. Guard against
   double-recording when the two paths overlap (e.g. keyed by `turn`).
3. **Persistence.** Serialise `turnStatsHistory`; on load, default to `[]`
   for legacy saves.
4. **Model.** Extend `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` with a pure
   series builder (e.g. `buildGameOverStatSeries(state)`) returning the five
   requested series plus the final "cash at end of turn" value.
5. **Render.** Add a **third column** to `showGameOverOverlay()` rendering the
   graphs via the chosen external charting library (encapsulated in a small
   helper module so the model stays Phaser-free and testable), and add the
   **Cash at end of turn** line plus a link to the stats column on the Summary
   column. Recompute `panelW` / column widths / `panelH` so all three columns
   fit the 1280×720 viewport.
6. **Guardrails.** Skip chart construction in `scene.replayMode` / headless
   mode; keep the pure model testable without booting Phaser or the chart
   library.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — Add `TurnStatSnapshot` + `turnStatsHistory`
  to `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — Initialise `turnStatsHistory: []` for
  single-player and competitive setups.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — Record the per-turn snapshot on both
  closing paths (reuse the `weekStartCoins`/`appendTurnNetRow` pattern).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — Serialise/restore `turnStatsHistory`
  with a legacy `[]` fallback.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — New pure series builder
  (`buildGameOverStatSeries`) + final cash-at-end-of-turn value.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — Third column rendering + Summary
  cash line + link; widen/rebalance the panel layout.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetStatsChart.ts` — **New** thin wrapper around the
  external charting library (skipped in replay/headless).
- `package.json` — Add the charting-library dependency.
- `tests/main-street/game-over-stats.test.ts` — **New** unit tests (capture,
  round-trip, legacy fallback, series model).
- `tests/main-street/game-over-overlay.test.ts` /
  `tests/main-street/game-over.browser.test.ts` — Third-column and cash-line
  assertions.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` / `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` —
  Document per-turn history and the end-of-game stats column.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM** – Provide reason for game ending (completed) — the
  epic that built the current Game Over overlay.
- **MS-0MUWE6NCA008LDXM** – Two-column Game Over overlay (completed) — the
  layout this item extends to a third column.
- **MS-0MUWE6MA30038RGY** – Game-over summary test harness (completed) — the
  fixture/helper pattern to reuse for tests.
- **MS-0MUWNTJIK009O6BZ** – Credit AI challenge completions to the AI seat
  (completed) — introduced the per-seat Game Over breakdown.
- **MS-0MUNB4ZXQ0081EX7** – Storyline coverage analytics in Monte Carlo
  harness (open) — consumes a per-turn economy series, the same shape this
  item persists.
- **Related docs:** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (§ Activity Log —
  Effective Deltas and Per-Turn Net, § Win conditions),

# Intake brief: Port the Vite watcher-ignore (`server.watch.ignored`) guard to sibling game repos' `vite.config.ts`

## Problem statement

The core scaffold template (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA) emits `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` (covering `**/.worklog/**` and the dev-output trees), and `tce-main-street` and `tce-the-rising` already carry the block — but 8 sibling game repos' checked-in `vite.config.ts` still lack it: `AI_Hell`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go`. When any of these repos accumulates `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (AI_Hell already has 9 + a nested `ToneForge` checkout), the Vite/Vitest file watcher recursively walks them and exhausts the host `fs.inotify.max_user_watches` budget — `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers reached` — crashing the dev server and breaking test runs (the exact failure mode fixed in the parent item MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY).

## Users

- **Developers/agents working in any Tableau-Card-Engine game repo** (tce-\*) — must be able to run `npm run dev` and `npm test` from the main checkout once worktrees exist without tripping the host watcher limit.
  - *User story:* "As a developer in tce-blackjack, I want my dev server to ignore `.worklog/worktrees/**` so a recursive watch never exhausts inotify (ENOSPC)."
- **AI_Hell maintainers** (in scope — Q1 answered) — same failure mode is already active (9 worktree checkouts).
  - *User story:* "As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same watcher guard, so my `vite` dev server survives `.worklog/worktrees/**` growth."
- **Verification/audit tooling** — full-suite runs in sibling repos must not fail with ENOSPC.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Watcher guard present in every in-scope repo's checked-in config.** The 7 tce-\* repos each import `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` from `./core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin` and set `server.watch.ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS]` with the template's explanatory comment (wording as in CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA / `tce-the-rising`). AI_Hell (if in scope) sets `watch.ignored` from a locally defined constant covering `**/.worklog/**` (plus its dev-output trees). Verified per repo by grep of the checked-in file — no in-scope repo may lack the block.
2. **Per-repo regression guard test (mirrors the core/main-street ENOSPC guard).** Each tce-\* repo gains `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (copy of main-street's, minus the in-process dev-server smoke; static assertions only): the real config imports the shared list, spreads it into `server.watch.ignored`, and the list covers `**/.worklog/**` plus `**/data/**`, `**/tmp/**`, `**/results/**`, `**/dist/**`. AI_Hell gains `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` asserting its local list covers `.worklog`. Each test is picked up by that repo's existing test projects and passes.
3. **Surgical port only.** No other template drift is synced: no `resolvePagesBase`/`base` backfill, no blind re-scaffold (sibling configs predate those template additions), no local-config changes (e.g. AI_Hell's `configCsvPlugin`, `open: true`, port settings) altered. Per-repo `git diff` touches only `vite.config.ts` plus the new guard test; pre-existing unrelated working-tree changes (`.gitignore`, untracked `AGENTS.md`/`.githooks/`/`.worklog/plugins/`) are never swept into a commit.
4. **Suites pass and changes land on each repo's `dev`.** Each in-scope repo's own test suite passes (agent-initiated runs go through the test skill, per repo), and each repo's change is committed on its `dev` branch and pushed to origin, with commits referencing `MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0` (precedent: cross-repo item MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV). The pre-existing 1-ahead-unpushed local commit on each sibling `dev` is accounted for at push time (see Constraints). tce-main-street itself has no source changes, so its suite is unaffected; full project suite (each modified repo) must pass with the changes.
5. **Documentation reflects the guard.** Config comment matches the core template wording; where a repo documents `npm run dev` (README/dev docs — currently none of the in-scope repos has a README), a matching note about the `.worklog/**` exclusion. CHANGELOG.md excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **No core/TCE repository edits and no submodule moves.** The core scaffold template and its guard tests are already correct (CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA completed) and every sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` in `scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` — verified.
- **Surgical only** — do **not** blind re-scaffold (`npm run scaffold` / `scaffold:games`): the current template additionally emits `resolvePagesBase`/production `base` behaviour that the sibling configs do not have; a re-scaffold would change more than the watch block. Port the `server.watch.ignored` block + import only.
- **Cross-repo working-tree isolation.** This item lives in tce-main-street's worklog but touches 8 sibling checkouts, all outside the tce-main-street worktree. Precedent MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV ("Cross-repo change ... Pushed to sibling dev") governs: edit each sibling checkout directly, commit per repo on its own `dev`, push per repo. tce-main-street's own worktree/main checkout stays untouched (no tce-main-street source change → no implement-worktree changes expected).
- **Respect pre-existing dirt.** Each sibling has unrelated uncommitted changes (`.gitignore` edits; untracked `AGENTS.md`, `.githooks/`, `.worklog/plugins/`). Never commit them; stage only `vite.config.ts` (+ new test).
- **Sibling `dev` is 1 commit ahead of origin** (an unpushed `.worklog/config.yaml` CTA commit, `WL-0MUWCGF670087GAS`). Pushing the port will carry that commit; if a non-fast-forward/push rejection occurs, resolve against that known baseline (do not rewrite others' pushed history).
- **Test-execution policy:** all agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill — run per repo (each sibling has its own CWD/worklog), never ad-hoc `npm test`/`vitest`.

## Existing state

- **Scaffolded siblings (7):** `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-golf`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-sushi-go` — `vite.config.ts` is AUTO-GENERATED (scaffold `renderViteConfig`), identical to each other apart from the game name in the header comment, and each `server:` block has `port: 3000, open: false` only — no `watch.ignored`. Verified: `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` absent from all 7.
- **AI_Hell (1):** bespoke hand-written config (port 5173, `open: true`, `configCsvPlugin`, no `core` submodule) — no `server.watch` at all; it **cannot** import the core list. It already has 9 `.worklog/worktrees/**` checkouts (+ nested `ToneForge` checkout) — the ENOSPC failure mode is live there.
- **Exemplars:** `tce-main-street/vite.config.ts` and `tce-the-rising/vite.config.ts` already carry the block (main-street also has `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`, the regression pattern to mirror; core has `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` static guard).
- Siblings' core submodules are clean and pinned at `v0.1.17-201-g09723c4b`, which exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`. Their `npm test` = `vitest run --project unit` with `include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']`, and tsconfig includes `tests/**/*.ts` — new config tests are picked up automatically.

## Desired change

- **Per tce-\* repo:** in `vite.config.ts`, add `import { DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS } from './core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin';` and extend the `server:` block with `watch: { ignored: [...DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS] }` + the template's ENOSPC comment; add `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (static assertions copied from main-street's guard).
- **AI_Hell (in scope — Q1 answered):** add a locally defined ignore constant (e.g. `vite/watchIgnore.ts`) mirroring the core list (or a scoped `.worklog`-focused list), wire `server: { watch: { ignored: [...] } }` into `vite.config.ts`, and add `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts`.
- Single source of truth stays in core; nothing in `core/` changes.

## Key Files:

- Each tce-\* repo: `vite.config.ts` — add `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` import + `server.watch.ignored` block
- Each tce-\* repo: `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (new) — static config-wiring + pattern-coverage guard (mirror of `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` ENOSPC assertions and main-street's `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts`)
- AI_Hell: `vite.config.ts` — wire `watch.ignored`; `vite/watchIgnore.ts` (new) — local ignore constant; `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (new) — guard test (AI_Hell test roots: `src`, `scripts`, `vite`)
- Reference only (no change): `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` (template already correct), `core/scripts/vite-transcript-plugin.ts` (`DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` source), `tce-main-street/tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` (guard pattern to mirror)

## Related work

- MS-0MV8M9IAF000KPNY — Host inotify watcher exhaustion (ENOSPC) breaks main-checkout test runs (**parent; completed**; this item is its derived sibling port)
- CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA — core: `game-repo-scaffold` renderViteConfig omits `server.watch.ignored` (completed; template now emits it)
- CG-0MTJ7A4Z3000MFMV / CG-0MTJ560IZ005XAZC — core: vite-transcript-plugin ENOSPC hardening (completed)
- MS-0MVA50KJN009X30C — [test-failure] suite-exit failure (completed; same root cause family)
- MS-0MV5PNIPO00940KG — Main Street vite-node CLI test flake (completed; the local isolation that a blind re-scaffold would regress)
- MS-0MUQ5A7N1008ORJV — Cross-repo change precedent: tracked in main-street worklog, "Pushed to sibling dev" AC (completed)
- MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV / MS-0MUQZH53F004ZKAN — Core scaffold Pages-base work (completed; the template drift deliberately **not** backfilled here)
- Note: sibling repos have their own worklog stores (some without a DB on disk); no sibling-side work items exist for this change — the main-street item is the tracking point.

## Assumptions & risks

- **Assumption (Q1 answered: include AI_Hell):** AI_Hell is in scope, handled via a locally defined ignore constant because it has no `core` submodule from which to import the shared list.
- **Risk (low):** chokidar ignore-glob semantics — `**/.worklog/**` covers `.worklog/worktrees/**`; validated by the core regression suite and main-street's in-process smoke. Sibling guards use the same static assertions.
- **Risk (medium):** list duplication in AI_Hell drifts from core over time — mitigation: comment in `vite/watchIgnore.ts` pointing at the core source (single source of truth), and the guard test pins `.worklog` coverage.
- **Risk (medium):** per-repo dev-server smoke tests ×8 would be slow/flaky under suite contention — mitigation: ship **static** config-wiring guards per repo (mirroring `game-repo-scaffold.test.ts`); the in-process `server.watcher.getWatched()` smoke stays where it already exists (main-street) — no new dev-server startups in siblings.
- **Risk (low):** push non-fast-forward on 7 sibling `dev` branches (each 1 local commit ahead of origin) — known baseline commit; rebase/stacking acceptable since those commits are local-only; surface anything unexpected rather than force-pushing.
- **Scope-creep risk:** syncing other stale template drift (`resolvePagesBase`/production `base`, `unit-cli` isolations, etc.) to siblings, or host inotify tuning, is tempting — recorded as related work (MS-0MUQZH5PH001JXLV etc.), NOT this item's scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: **Is AI_Hell in scope?** Its `vite.config.ts` is hand-written (not scaffold-generated), it has no `core` submodule, so the shared `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS` list cannot be imported — the port there requires a locally duplicated ignore constant (drift risk), though its failure mode is already live (9 worktrees).

- Research summary: verified all 8 repos lack the block (grep of checked-in configs); the 7 tce-\* configs are otherwise identical scaffold output (only the game name differs); each sibling's pinned core commit (`09723c4b`) already exports `DEV_WATCH_IGNORE_PATTERNS`; `tce-the-rising` is the wired exemplar; main-street's `tests/deploy/vite-watch-ignore-enospc.test.ts` is the guard pattern to mirror; AI_Hell's test roots are `src`/`scripts`/`vite` with an exhaustive project-membership classifier (vite/ test auto-classified as unit). ## Plan

**Decomposition (8 parallel children — one per in-scope repo).** Each child is a
vertical slice through all layers for its repo: config wiring + regression guard

All children are independent (no dependency edges) — each repo's port is

# Intake Brief — End of Turn summary dialog for competitive mode (MS-0MVO1SFCM000ZLBI)

## Problem statement

The single-player End of Turn summary dialog (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) gives the
player a deliberate review-and-advance moment after each turn. Competitive
(human-vs-AI) play has no equivalent: after the shared day's closing
presentation (`presentCompetitiveClosing`) the day auto-advances with only the
transient per-seat income text (`Player 1: +X coins | Player 2: +Y coins`, via
`perSeatClosingSummary`) and the incident reveal. There is no moment to compare
each seat's standing for the round just completed — businesses owned, income
and expenses per seat. This item extends the End of Turn summary dialog to
competitive mode: one panel per completed round (one shared day where every
seat finished and the closing ran), with **owner-keyed rows** (businesses
owned, income/expenses per seat).

## Users

- **Main Street competitive player (human seat)** — plays week-by-week against
  AI seats on the shared street; after each shared day's animations finish,
  wants a persistent panel showing every seat's round result and a deliberate
  "start the next day" action (parity with the single-player dialog).

**User stories:**

- As a competitive player, when the shared day's closing animations finish, I
  see one panel summarising the round with a row per seat (businesses owned,
  income, expenses, net change, closing coins/reputation/score) so I can
  compare standings and learn from the round.
- As a competitive player, I click **[ Next Turn ]** to start the next shared
  day — the day does not advance until I do.
- As a competitive player, I see the same (disabled) **[ Bank Loan ]**
  affordance as the single-player dialog, so the loans option is planned and
  consistent across modes.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In competitive play (N ≥ 2), after the shared closing presentation completes, a Turn Summary dialog appears with one panel per completed round — one owner-keyed row per non-eliminated seat showing businesses owned, income (with the per-phase breakdown), ongoing expenses per category (staff / community / business), net coin change, and closing coins / reputation / score; the next shared day does **not** start until the player clicks **[ Next Turn ]**, and reduced-motion, replay and headless/AI-driven paths skip the dialog and keep the existing auto-advance pacing.
2. The dialog content is **engine-computed and owner-keyed**: the competitive close surfaces per-seat ongoing costs, businesses owned and net change on `TurnResult` (extending the parent item's owner-keyed ledger design), so every value shown is testable without a browser and consistent with the single-player ledger; additions are optional and backwards-compatible — `MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn`, `presentCompetitiveClosing` and the headless/Monte-Carlo paths are unaffected when the field is absent.
3. # Intake brief: Remove broken `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` npm scripts from generated game repos

**Type:** chore · **Priority:** low · **Cross-repo:** yes (Tableau-Card-Engine core via the `./core` submodule) · **Discovered-from:** MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL

## Problem statement

Every generated game repo (`tce-main-street`, `tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, …) declares two npm scripts — `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` — that point at `tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, a file that does **not** exist in a game repo (Option C: game repos have no root `scripts/` tree; the scaffold lives in the core at `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`). Invoking either script fails with a module-not-found error. The working game-repo entry point, `npm run scaffold`, passes `--core-root ./core` and exists in every generated repo.

Root cause (resolved): `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` inherits the **entire** core `scripts` map from the core manifest (line ~280: `...Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(manifest.scripts ?? {}))`). `core/package.json` legitimately declares `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` for core-repo use, so both leak unmodified into every generated game repo. The description's open "which is true" question is answered: the template **does** emit them, but only by inheritance — the fix is a template-side filter, not merely deleting two lines from each repo.

## Users

- **Game-repo maintainers (agents and humans)** — run npm scripts inside a game repo without tripping over dead entries.
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of tce-main-street, I want `npm run scaffold:game` to either work or not be declared, so a script listed in my repo never fails with module-not-found."
- **Core scaffold owners (Tableau-Card-Engine)** — keep the template emitting only what a game repo can actually run.
  - *User story:* "As a core template owner, I want the scaffold to filter core-only scripts (including any future ones) out of generated repos, so a re-scaffold never reintroduces broken entries."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **This repo's `package.json` no longer declares `scaffold:game` or `scaffold:games`.** `npm run scaffold` remains and resolves to `tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street ...`. Guarded by a regression test (new `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts`) asserting the two broken keys are absent and every `scaffold*` script's target file exists.
2. **The scaffold template stops emitting them.** `renderPackageJson` in `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` filters the core-only `scaffold:game`/`scaffold:games` entries out of the inherited scripts map. Add a unit test in `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` whose manifest declares both keys and asserts the rendered `package.json` omits them, so a re-scaffold cannot reintroduce them (AC2 of the original item).
3. **The core change is delivered.** `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` + its test land in Tableau-Card-Engine (CG work item, per the MS↔CG pairing precedent of MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED↔CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q); this repo records the engine commit via its `./core` submodule pointer bump (`npm run engine:sync`), and `npm run scaffold` on a fixture checkout regenerates a `package.json` without the two keys.
4. **Documentation.** `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` documents `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo scaffold entry point and states that `scaffold:game(s)` are core-checkout-only commands; no game-repo-context doc references `scaffold:game(s)`. Core docs that use them (DEVELOPER.md, dev/creating-a-new-game.md, dev/multi-repo-architecture.md) are core-checkout context and remain accurate; a one-line "run from the core checkout" clarification is made where ambiguity exists.
5. **Validation.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes (changed-scope test gate plus the added regression tests; core-side suite green in the engine repo). The new `tests/tooling/` file is collected by the existing `unit` project (`tests/**/*.test.ts`, `vite.config.ts:222`) — no project-config change needed.

> **Traceability to the original ACs:** brief AC1 ← original AC1; brief AC2 + AC3 ← original AC2 ("resolve which is true first" resolved: the template emits them by inheritance, so a template filter is required); brief AC4 ← original AC3; brief AC5 ← original AC4.

## Constraints

- **Cross-repo delivery** — the template fix lives in the Tableau-Card-Engine repo (`core/` submodule); this item cannot satisfy AC2 in-repo. Push policy applies to both repos: `dev` only.
- **No `npm run scaffold` against the live checkout** — re-scaffolding this repo today **drops 10 locally-added scripts** (`docs`, `docs:build`, `docs:preview`, `pretest`, `test:browser`, `generate:pack-assets`, `validate:storylines`, `storylines:graph:svg`, `docs:diagrams`, `balance:synergy-diversity-report`) because the template does not preserve repo-local extras. AC1 must be done with a hand edit; fixture-based re-scaffold verification lives in tests.
- **No CI beyond npm builds** — the npm build/test scripts are the verification vehicle.
- Implementation follows the mandatory worktree + build→test→commit order of the implement skill; work-item tracking via wl only.

## Existing state

- Issue type stays `chore`: the change removes dead config keys and adjusts the scaffold's config generation; it changes no runtime app behaviour (matches the `discovered-from` item's classification).

- `package.json` (this repo, lines 34–35): `"scaffold:game": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts"`, `"scaffold:games": "tsx scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --all --core-root . --repos-dir .."`. Root `scripts/` contains only `run-tests.ts` and `soak-browser-waits.sh` — the target does not exist.
- `package.json` line 50: `"scaffold": "tsx ./core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core"` — the working entry point (exists in all sibling repos too).
- `core/package.json` lines 31–32 declare the same two scripts **validly** (core has `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` `renderPackageJson` (lines ~274–312) inherits all core scripts, then overrides repo entry points; `scaffold:game(s)` pass through unchanged.
- 9 sibling game repos (`../tce-golf`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-coloretto`, `tce-feudalism`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-f5-verify`, `tce-fresh-verify`, `tce-repos-f9`) carry the same two broken lines — separate repositories, out of scope for this item's ACs (see Follow-ups).
- Related inherited-scripts bug of the same class: 8 more core-only entries arrive broken in every game repo (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — the last breaks `npm run package`/`package:win|linux|mac`). Excluded from scope (see Follow-ups).

## Desired change

1. Remove `scaffold:game` and `scaffold:games` from this repo's root `package.json` (hand edit; see Constraints).
2. In `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`, filter the core-only keys out of the inherited scripts map — a small explicitly-named drop-list (or drop any inherited script that still references the core-only `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` target) with a comment explaining the Option C no-root-`scripts/` rationale and pointing at the follow-up item for the broader class.
3. Add/extend unit tests on both sides; bump the `./core` submodule pointer to the engine commit carrying the template fix.
4. Update `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` (and the one-line core-doc clarification in Tableau-Card-Engine).

## Key Files

- `package.json` — remove the two `scaffold:game(s)` entries (this repo).
- `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `renderPackageJson`: drop core-only inherited scripts (template fix, engine repo).
- `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — extend MANIFEST fixture with `scaffold:game(s)` and assert they are omitted from the rendered `package.json`.
- `tests/tooling/scaffold-scripts.test.ts` (new) — regression guard: no `scaffold:game(s)` declared; every `scaffold*` script target exists.
- `docs/dev/build-and-release.md` — document `npm run scaffold` as the game-repo entry point; note `scaffold:game(s)` are core-only.
- `.gitmodules` / `gitlink core` — submodule pointer bump to the engine commit with the template fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Dead-key approach is undocumented assumption.** Assumption (recorded, not operator-confirmed): the fix is the narrow one from the item title — drop only `scaffold:game(s)`; the other 8 broken inherited scripts are a separate discovered follow-up (below). If the operator prefers the general filter (fixes all 10), AC1–AC5 grow; flagged, not blocking.
- **R2 — Submodule bump pulls unrelated engine commits.** The engine `dev` head is ahead of the pinned submodule (pinned `9ee194e0…` vs engine `dev` `1c9900a1…`). Mitigation: keep the bump to a reviewable commit; full suite must stay green (AC5).
- **R3 — Incomplete inheritance semantics.** Filtering only `scaffold:game(s)` is a stop-gap while the general class remains broken; over time more core-only scripts may be added. Mitigation: follow-up item tracks the general fix (`discovered-from` link).
- **R4 — Re-scaffold destructiveness discovered during intake.** If the template's preserve-on-re-scaffold behaviour is later expected to keep repo-local scripts, that is a separate enhancement — out of scope here.
- **Scope-creep guard:** sibling-repo clean-up, the 8-script general fix, and template local-script preservation are all recorded as follow-ups, not folded into this item.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** — "[test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts" (the `discovered-from` parent; same scaffold-template class of bug).
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED ↔ CG-0MVD0IZDR008921Q** — engine-sync wiring precedent: core template change (in engine repo) + game-repo side + re-scaffold; the MS↔CG pairing model this item follows.
- **CG-0MVGF2QE9008NA5R** — version policy in `renderPackageJson` (the same function being changed).
- **MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0** — sibling-repo port of a core template guard; same cross-repo pattern.
- **CG-0MV5SEHHG000ZKUA** — scaffold vite.config template ownership.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL** – [test-failure follow-up] Scaffold template must emit resolve.dedupe in generated vite.config.ts (open)
- **MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED** – Auto-sync engine submodule on dev builds; pin release builds to committed engine version (completed)
- **MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O** – Engine dev tip renamed the story-line docs seam section (game doc-drift test pinned old heading) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mvcrgkzy007died, ac4, appear, banner, broken (+68 more)
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: appear, banner, changes, context, core (+54 more)
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, appear (+50 more)
> Assessment: `MS-0MVK4TS31000YNFL` and `MS-0MVCRGKZY007DIED` are genuinely related (same template/entry-point class). `MS-0MVMNO29Z009SF6O` matched on keyword noise (story-line docs seam) and is **not** relevant to this item; repo-file matches are incidental IDF matches. Full untruncated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0.md`.

## Follow-ups (recorded; out of scope)

- **Generalise the inherited-scripts filter** to all core-only entries that reference the absent game-repo `scripts/` tree (`test:smoke`, `test:dev`, `context:check`, `context:refresh`, `replay`, `transcripts:export`, `tf:generate`, `build:electron-main` — `build:electron-main` breakage disables `npm run package*` in every game repo). `discovered-from: MS-0MVO30VXS002A1Z0`.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Headline:** Add a persisted *Auto advance turn* setting that either ends the day
automatically when the player can no longer act, or — when off (default) — explains the
out-of-actions state in a dialog that offers to turn the setting on.

## Problem statement

When a player has spent their last action point the game offers no explanation and no
shortcut to progress: they must notice the red `0 actions left` counter and find the
**End Turn** button themselves. Add a persisted **Auto advance turn** setting that
either ends the turn automatically or, when off (the default), explains the situation in
a dialog that also lets the player turn the setting on.

## Users

- **New / casual solo player** — does not yet know that a day ends only when they press
  **End Turn**, and does not know that some staff cards grant extra action points.
  - *As a new player who has just spent my last action, I want to be told why I can no
    longer act and how to continue, so that the game never feels stuck.*
  - *As a player who understands the loop, I want the turn to advance on its own once I
    have nothing left to do, so that I stop clicking End Turn 8+ times a game.*
- **Experienced player** — wants to opt in once and never see the dialog again.
- **Competitive player** — the same out-of-actions moment exists on a human seat during a
  shared day; auto-advance must hand the day to the AI seats exactly as a manual
  **End Turn** does.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Setting exists and is exposed in the settings menu.** A boolean preference
   (`Auto advance turn`) defaults to **false**, persists across sessions in
   `localStorage`, and is rendered as a toggle in the in-game Settings panel alongside the
   existing `Tooltips` / `Reduced Motion` toggles. Toggling it in either place (panel or
   dialog checkbox) updates the same stored preference.
2. **Auto advance on — trigger is the spent-last-action moment (producer decision, Q1 = B).**
   The trigger fires when the player's action budget reaches zero as an action resolves: after
   the action that spends the last action point, and only once that action's animations and
   audio have completed (never mid-animation). With the setting enabled the trigger performs
   the *same* operation as clicking **End Turn** — identical phase flow,
   income/incident/event-choice resolution, turn-summary presentation and save/checkpoint
   behaviour — and fires **at most once per turn** (no double advance, no re-entrant
   end-turn while `uiPhase === 'animating'`).
3. **Dialog when off — same trigger.** With the setting disabled the same spent-last-action
   trigger (again after animations/audio complete) opens a dialog that
   states the player has no action points left, that certain kinds of employed staff grant
   extra action points, and that they must break for the weekend by pressing **End Turn**.
   The dialog offers an **End Turn** button, a **Dismiss** affordance that returns the
   player to the market phase, and a checkbox (unchecked by default) reading
   `[ ] Automatically end my turn when I run out of actions`; checking it persists the
   preference immediately (so the next out-of-actions moment auto-advances).
4. **Non-intrusive.** The dialog fires at most once per turn (re-opening only on a later
   turn), is presented once the action's animations/audio have completed rather than on top
   of them, and never appears while a modal overlay (turn summary, loan offer, event
   choice) is already open. Dismissing it leaves the player in the market phase with the
   **End Turn** button available, so the action-free operations that remain after the last
   action (discarding a hand card, selling, researching the market, opening the journal)
   stay reachable for a player who declines the auto-advance.
5. **Mode guards.** Auto-advance never fires during the tutorial unless the current
   tutorial step is `end-turn` (respecting `isTutorialActionAllowed('end-turn')`), never
   while it is not the human seat's turn in competitive play, and never during
   `uiPhase` values where **End Turn** is not offered (e.g. `placing-from-hand`,
   `event-selected`, `applicant`).
6. **Tests.** Unit tests cover the preference default/persistence and the once-per-turn
   latch; browser tests cover (a) auto-advance ending the turn exactly once, (b) the
   dialog appearing when the setting is off, (c) the checkbox persisting the preference
   and the panel toggle reflecting it, (d) the tutorial/competitive guards, and (e) the
   trigger waiting for the last action's animation to complete.
7. **Documentation.** `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (settings toggle inventory) and
   `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 (action economy) are updated to describe
   the setting and the out-of-actions behaviour. All related documentation (code comments,
   README where relevant) is updated to reflect the changes.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **`core/` is a git submodule** of the Tableau Card Engine
  (`TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`, tracked branch `dev`, pinned by
  `configs/engine-pin.json`). The Settings panel lives in the engine
  (`core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, `core/src/ui/CardGameScene.ts`), so exposing the
  toggle there needs a **generic, game-agnostic** engine change (e.g. a
  `extraToggles?: { label, get, set }[]` config) committed in the engine repo, followed by
  an `npm run engine:sync` re-pin in this repo. Engine work must not hard-code Main Street
  concepts.
- Preference storage must follow the existing `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts` pattern
  (injectable `StorageLike`, best-effort failure handling) so unit tests run in Node.
- Dialog presentation must follow the existing overlay conventions used by
  `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` (backdrop depth 199, box 200, elements 201, registered in
  `s.overlayObjects`, parented into `hudContainer`) — no new ad-hoc depth values.
- Zero-action gating currently exists at several call sites
  (`MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions`, `MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop`,
  `MainStreetMarketSell`, `MainStreetMarketPurchase`). Those remain legality checks for
  illegal attempts; the new behaviour is a **single post-action trigger** and must not be
  duplicated per site.
- The trigger must run only after the triggering action's animations **and** audio have
  completed — it cannot be bolted onto the raw state mutation, because the player would
  see the turn end underneath a playing animation.
- CHANGELOG.md is out of scope (managed by the ship/release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts` already stores game-specific preferences in `localStorage`
  (`tce-main-street-buy-and-place-premium-dialog-dismissed`,
  `tce-main-street-enabled-card-packs`) with an injectable storage adapter.
- `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts` renders toggles for Mute, Tooltips, Reduced Motion,
  difficulty, card design, end-turn keybind and (dev-only) Debug Tools; the panel is
  configured through `SettingsPanelConfig` and created by
  `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel(...)`, which `MainStreetScene` overrides.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts#showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` is the closest
  precedent: a modal explainer with a persisted "Don't show this again" checkbox.
- Out-of-actions feedback today is a transient `flashError` string —
  `'No actions remaining this week. End your turn to start next week.'` — raised from
  `onBusinessCardClick`, `onMarketRefresh`, staff-move handlers, drag-drop guards and the
  market legality helpers.
- The HUD shows `N actions left (M banked)` in the action cluster above the **End Turn**
  button; the End Turn handler is `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` →
  `endTurn(tcCtx)` in `MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts`, which already implements the
  tutorial gate, the banking hint and the competitive hand-off.
- Playing with zero actions is still deliberately possible at a premium (same-turn
  buy-and-place costs +50%), and several operations are action-free (discard, sell,
  research market, journal).

## Desired change

1. `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts`: add `tce-main-street-auto-advance-turn` with
   `isAutoAdvanceTurnEnabled()` / `setAutoAdvanceTurnEnabled(enabled, storage?)`.
2. A single out-of-actions hook driven by the **post-action** path (producer decision
   Q1 = B): after an action resolves and its animations/audio complete, if the player's
   `actionsRemaining` has reached 0, then
   - setting **on** → invoke the same code path as the **End Turn** button, guarded by a
     once-per-turn latch and by the mode/phase guards in AC5;
   - setting **off** → `showOutOfActionsDialog()` once per turn.
   The existing per-site `actionsRemaining <= 0` legality guards
   (`MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions`, `MainStreetTurnControllerDragDrop`,
   `MainStreetMarketSell`, `MainStreetMarketPurchase`) stay as they are — they remain the
   legality check for illegal attempts, not the trigger.
3. `MainStreetOverlayContent.showOutOfActionsDialog()` — explainer copy, an **End Turn**
   button, and an `[ ] Automatically end my turn when I run out of actions` checkbox that
   writes the preference when ticked.
4. Engine change (submodule): a generic extra-toggle hook in `SettingsPanelConfig` /
   `SettingsPanel` (and pass-through in `CardGameScene.initSettingsPanel`), wired from
   `MainStreetScene.initSettingsPanel` to the Main Street preference.
5. Tests and documentation as per AC6–AC7.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetPrefs.ts` — new `tce-main-street-auto-advance-turn` key + getter/setter,
  mirroring the premium-dialog preference pattern.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — new `showOutOfActionsDialog()` following
  `showBuyAndPlacePremiumDialog` (backdrop/box/element depths, checkbox + button,
  `overlayObjects` registration).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerUtils.ts` (or a new
  `src/scenes/MainStreetOutOfActions.ts`) — shared post-action out-of-actions helper +
  once-per-turn latch, called after an action's animation/audio settles.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` / `MainStreetAnimator*` — the
  animation-completion seam the trigger must wait on (the action is only "spent" for this
  purpose once its animations and audio have finished).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — call the post-action hook after
  each successful action resolution; leave the existing zero-action `flashError` guards
  untouched.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — extend the `initSettingsPanel` override to pass the
  auto-advance toggle.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — panel initialisation site
  (`s.initSettingsPanel(DIFFICULTY_NAMES, 'Medium')`) if the toggle is wired there.
- `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts`, `core/src/ui/CardGameScene.ts` — generic
  `extraToggles` config (engine repo, submodule pin bump via `npm run engine:sync`).
- `tests/main-street/main-street-prefs.test.ts` — preference unit tests.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetAutoAdvanceTurn.browser.test.ts` (new) — auto-advance,
  dialog, checkbox persistence and guard browser tests.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (settings toggle inventory),
  `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 Action Economy.

## Related work

- `MS-0MUUDWIXG009IB0W` — *Reject illegal moves before animation and action-point
  deduction* (the gate-then-animate pattern the helper should reuse).
- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — *End of Turn summary dialog* (the modal that follows a turn
  ending; auto-advance must still present it).
- `MS-0MVWMDMLE007I8E1` — *Harden Help/Settings browser tests* (Settings panel test
  conventions).
- `MS-0MT24X0SX007RLHN` — buy-and-place premium explainer dialog (the closest UI
  precedent, and the interaction that keeps zero-action play meaningful).
- `MS-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR` — action tooltip / action economy documentation.
- Duplicate check performed (`wl search` for "end turn", "action points", "settings") — no
  overlapping item satisfies these acceptance criteria.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk.** "Auto advance" invites extra wishes (auto-advance after N idle
  seconds, a countdown timer, auto-end in tutorial). These are recorded as follow-up work
  items, not folded in here.
- **Documented trade-off (producer decision Q1 = B).** Triggering on the spent-last-action
  moment means an opted-in player cannot use the action-free operations or the +50%
  same-turn buy-and-place after their final action — the turn simply ends. This is the
  intended behaviour of the opt-in setting; with the setting **off** the dialog is
  dismissible and those options stay reachable (AC4). If playtesting shows the trade-off
  is too harsh, a follow-up could defer the trigger while the hand has discardable cards or
  a premium placement is affordable — recorded as a follow-up, not in scope here.
- **Cross-repo coupling.** The Settings-panel toggle requires an engine change plus a
  submodule pin bump; the pin policy (`docs/dev/build-and-release.md`) means the engine
  commit must land on the engine `dev` branch before this repo's build is reproducible.
- **Re-entrancy.** Auto-advance runs from inside input handlers that already animate; it
  must be latched per turn, must wait for the triggering action's animations/audio to
  complete, and must not fire while `uiPhase === 'animating'` or while a dialog/overlay is
  open (turn-summary, loan offer, event choice).
- **Assumption:** the dialog is a one-off explainer (once per turn, and only while the
  setting is off), not a permanent nag on every illegal click.
- **Assumption:** the setting is global (per player), not per save game — it is a UI
  preference like Reduced Motion, not game state, so it is not serialised into saves.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Intake was auto-dispatched with no interactive producer present, so the three decisions
below were recorded on the work item as a comment and the item flagged for producer review.
All three were subsequently answered by the producer (source: interactive reply,
2026-11-05) — **Q1 = B, Q2 = A, Q3 = A** — and the brief above reflects those answers.

- **Q1 — When exactly does the out-of-actions moment fire?** Options: (A) when the player
  attempts an action that costs an action point while at zero (replacing today's
  `flashError`); (B) immediately after the action that spends the last point resolves;
  (C) both (B for auto-advance, A for the dialog).
  **Recommended: A** — it preserves the deliberate zero-action affordances (discard, sell,
  research market, +50% same-turn buy-and-place) and gives one deterministic trigger that
  replaces the existing error path.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): B — "immediately after the action that spends the last
  action point resolves", with the qualification "and any animations/audio have completed".**
  Prior recommendation (A) superseded; the resulting trade-off is documented under *Risks
  and assumptions*.
- **Q2 — How should the setting be surfaced in the Settings panel?** Options: (A) a
  generic `extraToggles` hook in the engine's `SettingsPanel` (engine repo change + pin
  bump), consumed by Main Street; (B) a Main Street-owned settings overlay outside the
  engine panel; (C) engine-side `hasAutoAdvanceTurn` flag.
  **Recommended: A** — keeps the engine game-agnostic, reuses the existing panel, and is
  reusable by other games.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): A** — matches the recommendation.
- **Q3 — Which modes, and how often may the dialog appear?** Options: (A) solo + competitive
  human seats, suppressed in the tutorial and once per turn; (B) solo only; (C) all modes
  including the tutorial.
  **Recommended: A** — the tutorial's scripted `end-turn` steps would dead-end under
  auto-advance, and a per-turn nag would be hostile.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-11-05): A** — matches the recommendation.
## Related work (automated report)

- **MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R** – Gating: wire turn summary into finishTurnPresentation (completed)
- **MS-0MVRNV9Y8008IKGK** – Competitive summary rows end-to-end (open)

# Colour of service businesses

## Problem statement

Service businesses render in a dark purple that is visually indistinguishable
from the flat purple face used by every upgrade card, so the two card families
read as the same thing at a glance on the street and in hand. At the same
time, an upgrade card carries no information about *what* it upgrades: all 39
upgrade cards share one uniform purple face regardless of the business they
apply to.

## Users

- **Main Street player** (primary) — scanning their hand and the market needs
  to distinguish a service business from an upgrade card instantly, and to see
  which family of business an upgrade belongs to without reading its title.
  - *As a player, I want service businesses in a colour no other card family
    uses, so I never mistake a service business for an upgrade card.*
  - *As a player, I want each upgrade card to show the colour of the business
    family it upgrades, so I can pick a relevant upgrade from my hand without
    reading every title.*

- **Colour-blind player** — the distinction must not rely on hue alone; the
  checkered pattern is itself a non-colour cue, and the upgrade card keeps its
  title and "for <Business>" target text.

## Existing state

- Synergy-type card faces are coloured from two parallel palettes:
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE` (dark faces, `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and the
  bright `synergyColor` accent palette. The static Node generator
  (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) duplicates both; an
  existing test asserts the two copies of the face palette agree
  (MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4).
- Service currently holds dark purple `#6A1B9A` (face) / `0x9B59B6` (accent).
- Upgrade cards are flat purple: background `#6B4C9A`, accent `#9B59B6`,
  rendered by `generateUpgradeCardSvg` / `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and by
  `cardColorScheme` / the family branch in the `.mjs` generator.
- 39 upgrade rows in `src/card-data.csv` carry a `targetBusiness` name but no
  synergy column of their own; synergy must be resolved by looking the target
  name up among business **and** community-space rows (6 targets are community
  spaces: Community Garden, Health Kiosk, Library, Park, Playground, Town
  Fountain).
- 9 businesses are bridge cards with two synergy types; 11 upgrade rows target
  them (Cafe, Food Truck, Art Gallery, Day Spa, Flower Shop, Juice Bar, Yoga
  Studio, Teahouse).

## Desired change

1. **New service colour.** Replace Service's palette entries with a pink /
   magenta that no other synergy type uses, in **both** palettes (face and
   accent) and in **both** copies (TypeScript and the `.mjs` duplicate), so the
   palette-agreement test still passes.
2. **Checkered upgrade faces.** Upgrade card faces become a checkerboard of
   violet and the synergy colour of the business the upgrade targets, instead
   of the current flat purple.
3. **Bridge targets use both colours.** When the upgrade targets a card with
   two synergy types, the checkerboard uses both synergy colours (with violet
   in the remaining squares).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The Service synergy type's face colour is a pink/magenta distinct from
      every other synergy colour, applied in `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`
      (`src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts`) and its `.mjs` duplicate
      (`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`); the existing
      TS/mjs palette-agreement test passes unchanged in intent.
- [ ] The bright Service accent colour (`synergyColor`) is updated to the
      matching pink/magenta family so icons, header tint and art backing stay
      consistent (the `expanded-card-pool` assertion is updated to the new
      value).
- [ ] A generated upgrade card face renders as a checkerboard of violet and
      the target's synergy colour, for both the runtime generator
      (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` / `generateUpgradeCardSvg`) and the static
      `.mjs` generator, with both paths producing the same pattern.
- [ ] An upgrade targeting a single-synergy business yields a two-colour
      checkerboard (violet + that synergy colour).
- [ ] An upgrade targeting a bridge business (two synergy types) yields all
      three colours: violet plus **both** synergy colours.
- [ ] An upgrade whose target synergy cannot be resolved (unknown or missing
      target) degrades safely to the existing flat purple face and never
      throws.
- [ ] Upgrade cards remain legible: title, "for <Business>" target text, cost
      badge and art stay readable over the checkerboard (existing contrast
      expectations in the SVG tests are preserved).
- [ ] New unit tests cover: the new service colour, single-synergy
      checkerboard, bridge-target three-colour checkerboard, unresolvable
      target fallback, and TS/mjs pattern agreement.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The static Node generator runs outside the TS build and cannot import
  TypeScript modules, so any palette or resolver change must be duplicated
  there and kept in agreement (existing project pattern).
- Upgrade synergy colour must be **derived**, not added as a new CSV column:
  `targetBusiness` is the only link today, and adding data columns would
  invalidate CSV checksums and pack fixtures.
- Upgrade **card** faces change only. The in-game board upgrade accent (the
  gold corner shard on an upgraded business, `UpgradeOverlaySpec`) and the
  owner-coloured seat border are out of scope — they are a separate visual
  language and were deliberately settled by MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF.
- Card faces must remain readable at the reduced hand/stacked scale (the art
  zone and text column must not be masked by the pattern).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardsUtils.ts` — new Service entry in `synergyColor` and
  `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`; likely the natural home for a pure
  `upgradeFaceBackground(targetSynergyTypes)`-style resolver.
- `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` — duplicated palettes plus
  the `upgrade` family branch in `cardColorScheme`; mirror the checkerboard and
  the new service colour.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — `generateUpgradeCardSvg`,
  `generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` (upgrade branch) and `cardColorScheme`; emit the
  checkerboard rect group (mirroring the existing `cardFaceSplitSvg` approach,
  possibly generalised into a checker tile helper).
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` — re-export any new resolver alongside
  `cardFaceBackground`.
- `src/card-data.csv` — read-only reference: `targetBusiness` values are the
  lookup keys; no schema change expected.
- `tests/main-street/mjs-svg-generator.test.ts` — palette-agreement and static
  render-path tests; extend for the checkerboard.
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — runtime SVG generator tests;
  add upgrade-face cases.
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — asserts the Service accent
  value; update to the new colour.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUZH51PU007POJ4 — Colour card faces by synergy type (two-tone bridge
  cards)** (completed) — established `CARD_FACE_PALETTE`, `cardFaceBackground`
  and the TS/mjs palette-agreement test this item builds on.
- **MS-0MUWNTN8W006C7EF — Identify different AI players** (completed) — moved
  upgrade state to the owner-coloured border + top-left accent; constrains the
  board visual language this item must not disturb.
- **MS-0MVZC5V6L001OOXN — Upgrade highlights should only be the current
  player's businesses** (completed) — upgrade targeting/placement rendering;
